dedupe_keys.name: climate proofing social housing landscapes hammersmith and fulham london life

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the LIFE+ project Climate-Proofing Social Housing Landscapes (2013 to 2016), in which the charity Groundwork London and Hammersmith and Fulham Council retrofitted three social housing estates in west London with affordable, light-engineering green and blue infrastructure against surface water flooding and summer heat. Measures included sustainable drainage features, greening and other landscape changes, designed with residents and delivered partly through employment programmes for long-term unemployed people, with the aim of a transferable design method. The total budget was 1.6 million euro, half from LIFE+, and the adaptation measures cost 526,000 euro: 297,000 euro at the Queen Caroline Estate, 137,000 euro at the Cyril Thatcher, Richard Knight and Eric MacDonald Houses and 92,000 euro at Cheeseman's Terrace. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: results are reported by the project, performance monitoring is limited, and the estates are small. It illustrates climate adaptation through retrofit of sustainable drainage and greening in dense housing; a related record is the EPA National Stormwater Calculator.
